root_cause.text: The TPM device teardown path in `tpm_dev_release()` freed the `chip->auth` `struct tpm2_auth` with plain `kfree()` instead of `kfree_sensitive()`, so HMAC session secrets, nonces, and passphrase data remained uncleared in freed slab memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `kfree(chip->auth);` to `kfree_sensitive(chip->auth);` in `drivers/char/tpm/tpm-chip.c`, and the CVE text states this was the only free path for `chip->auth` that did not zero sensitive cryptographic material before release.

intent_record.intent_summary: Wipe TPM HMAC authentication data before freeing it in the device release path.
intent_record.what: In tpm_dev_release(), the deallocation of chip->auth under CONFIG_TCG_TPM2_HMAC was changed from kfree(chip->auth) to kfree_sensitive(chip->auth).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the auth buffer will now be wiped before being freed, so TPM authentication-related data is less likely to remain in freed memory and be exposed through reuse or inspection.
